title: The Hormuz 'Deal' Is a Standstill — Iran's Ban Plan vs. AIS Traffic Data
narrative: The Trump administration insists a deal with Iran is effectively done. Trump called off planned strikes and said 'the outlines of a deal had already been settled' with Tehran. In the Oval Office he claimed the conflict will end 'pretty soon.' Senior US officials said talks had progressed far enough for shipments to potentially resume 'later this week.' But Iran's parliament speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf calls it 'theater diplomacy on loop.' Tehran says no talks are underway. Instead, Iran's parliament is reviewing a draft plan that would BAN US- and Israeli-linked ships from the Strait and levy penalties of up to 20% of cargo value on violators. Kpler vessel-tracking data shows only TWO vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday — against a pre-war baseline of roughly 130-140 daily transits. The waterway is not reopening. It is emptying.
telemetry: Trump Oval Office claim: conflict will end 'pretty soon'; 'the outlines of a deal had already been settled' with Tehran
Senior US officials: shipments could resume 'later this week'
Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf (X, Thu 6 Aug): 'Massive attack coming … wait, never mind, they want to negotiate. That's theater diplomacy on loop'
Iran foreign ministry: traffic-management framework with Oman 'in final stages' but 'would not automatically reopen the waterway'
Deputy FM Gharibabadi: any route would be temporary (2-4 months)
Iran parliament draft plan (Fars): BAN US- and Israeli-linked ships from the Strait; penalties of up to 20% of cargo value on violators
Kpler AIS data: 2 vessels transited Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 8 previous day — pre-war baseline ~130-140/day
Bab el-Mandeb: single dry bulk carrier transit, down from 20 vessels previous day
Brent October futures +1.3% to $83.55/bbl; WTI September +1.1% to $78.17 on Friday as ban plan circulated
US imports of Saudi crude dropped to ZERO in July — first time since 1985 (UOB note via CNBC)
Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in Gulf of Aden
Saudi official (CNN): kingdom bracing for 'multiple coordinated attacks' by Iraq-based militia factions and Iran-backed Houthis
Baqaei: insecurity 'still exist[s]' due to US naval blockade of Iranian ports
No route coordinates published; no tanker confirmed loading at Gulf terminal
analysis:
The White House is running a diplomatic narrative that cannot survive contact with AIS vessel-tracking data. Every time the administration announces progress — 'the outlines of a deal,' 'shipments resume this week' — the Strait of Hormuz empties further. Two vessels on Wednesday is not a waterway reopening. It is a waterway functionally closed, sustained by nothing more than the handful of tankers too far along to turn back.

The contradiction is not between the US and Iran. It is between the White House and observable reality. Kpler's data is commercially available, independently verifiable, and updated daily. The pre-war baseline of 130-140 transits per day is well-established. The collapse to 2 vessels is not ambiguous. It is a 98.5% traffic reduction that has persisted for months. If 'the outlines of a deal' were actually settled, tanker captains — who insure their hulls, their cargo, and their crews — would already be moving. They are not.

Iran's parliamentary ban plan makes the contradiction explicit. The 'deal' the White House describes — free transit, resumed shipments — is the opposite of what Iran's legislature is drafting. A ban on US- and Israeli-linked vessels, enforced with 20% cargo-value penalties, is not a negotiated settlement. It is a legislative codification of the blockade. Ghalibaf's 'theater diplomacy on loop' is not rhetorical flourish. It is a description of a pattern: the US announces a deal, Iran denies one, AIS data confirms Iran's denial, and the cycle repeats.

Markets have learned to read the pattern. Brent crude rose on Friday specifically because the ban plan circulated — reversing an earlier slide on 'deal in days' headlines. The market is pricing Tehran's position, not Washington's. The zero Saudi crude imports into the US in July — the first such month since 1985 — is not a diplomatic milestone. It is physical evidence that the waterway remains closed regardless of what the White House says.

The timeline mismatch is structural, not accidental. US officials say 'talks progressed → shipments resume this week.' Tehran says no negotiations exist. No route coordinates have been published. No tanker has been confirmed loading. Observed transits fell to 2/day. These four data points cannot all be true simultaneously. Three of them are verifiable. One — the White House claim — is not.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: The 'deal is days away' narrative is a diplomatic loop, not a settlement. Every time the White House announces progress, AIS data shows the Strait emptying further (2 transits/day vs. 130-140 baseline). Iran's parliamentary ban plan codifies the blockade — not the reopening. Markets are pricing Tehran's position, not Washington's. US Saudi crude imports at zero since July is the physical proof: the waterway is closed, and no amount of Oval Office optimism has changed that.
